scope: Representative expansion/update of Fig.17 of arXiv:2412.01535. Not an exhaustive world average.
error_rule: Prefer a source-quoted total when provided; otherwise combine all quoted symmetric components in quadrature. Preserve asymmetric total intervals. Inner bars use only explicitly verified error_stat fields, with the same scale as the central value. Never combine results across studies.
selection_notes: Show recent representative results, not a world average. Omit superseded ETMC/PNDME results, the very uncertain RQCD strange result, and the nonphysical single-spacing chiQCD charm result. Historical records remain below for provenance. The two PNDME light analyses share data. Copeland fits published baryon masses and takes FH derivatives, without a continuum extrapolation. Liang instead reanalyzes Mainz sigma-term data using an FH-derived two-loop formula, and remains a separate chiral-reanalysis category in the light preview.

studies.method: Model-dependent extraction from J/psi photoproduction, exponential fit
studies.notes: Same data as kou24_dipole, not an independent determination. Quoted error is the spread over photon energies, not a full statistical/systematic budget. Model and parameter uncertainties are excluded. Retained for reference but excluded from the publication comparison because these theoretical uncertainties are not fully quantified.

studies.label: Copeland et al. (2023)
studies.locator: Table I, nucleon row and caption; Sec. III on absence of a continuum limit
studies.method: Feynman-Hellmann derivatives of SU(3) chiral fits with finite-range regularization to published lattice baryon masses
studies.notes: Reanalysis of PACS-CS and QCDSF-UKQCD mass data, not a new ensemble calculation or a continuum extrapolation. Errors in Table I: statistical, scale-setting prescription, higher-order theoretical uncertainty (10% for light, 20% for strange). All three belong in the total bar.
